title: Identity Disclosure
description: The wearable device (Process P1) shares raw sensor telemetry (heart rate, step counts, GPS position, timestamps) with the user (ExternalEntity EE1). This act of sharing causes the threat because the user, as an external entity, can link or identify the device owner through the metadata of the data being shared.
assumptions: The device is accessible to the user and the user has the capability to access the device.

title: Data-Linking Threat
description: The data flow (DF1) transmits raw sensor telemetry (heart rate, step counts, GPS position, timestamps) between the wearable device and the user. This data-centric threat arises because the raw data includes identifying metadata (timestamps, GPS coordinates) that can be used to link or identify the user and the device owner.
assumptions: The data is transmitted in a format that allows for identification or linking.

title: Data-Processing Threat
description: The wearable device (Process P1) processes the incoming sensor telemetry data (heart rate, step counts, GPS position, timestamps) to extract and store the user's location and activity patterns. This processing action causes the threat because the device stores the user's location data, which can be used to identify the user.
assumptions: The device stores the user's location data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Device (P1) shares personal data (exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, timestamps) with the Companion Mobile App (P2) via the data flow DF2. This constitutes a data disclosure as the device transfers personal data to a third party (the app) without a direct data store intermediary, fitting the definition of transfer to a known or unknown third party.
assumptions: The data is considered personal data as it includes GPS traces and device identifiers.

title: Linking via Meta-data
description: The data flow DF2 transmits meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., device ID, timestamps, exercise session IDs) in transit. This meta-data can be used to link or identify the specific individuals whose data is being shared, creating a data-centric threat.
assumptions: The app and device exchange metadata to establish the data flow.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) receives the personal data (exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, timestamps) and processes or stores it in a way that causes a threat. Storing GPS traces and device identifiers on a mobile device creates a risk of unauthorized access or misuse.
assumptions: The app stores the received data locally.

title: Unawareness as a user sharing personal data
description: The user (ExternalEntity EE1) does not need to be the data subject for the data to be processed. The user is merely a 'wearer' of the app and does not have direct control over the data they share, leading to a potential privacy breach if the app processes personal data without explicit consent.
assumptions: The user is unaware of the specific data being processed or the extent of the processing.

title: Data-centric threat: Meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them
description: The data flow DF3 involves the companion mobile app (Process P2) receiving data from the user (ExternalEntity EE1). The meta-data about the parties (User and Companion App) being used to link or identify them could be used to track the user's activity or profile, creating a data-centric threat.
assumptions: The data flow involves the transfer of personal data from the user to the app.

title: Data-centric threat: Processing or storing data in a way that causes the threat
description: The companion mobile app (Process P2) receives the user's calorie intake, meals, and weight entries. The processing or storage of this personal data by the app could cause a privacy threat if the app does not have appropriate safeguards or if the data is used inappropriately.
assumptions: The app processes personal data from the user.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app (Process P2) shares personal health data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) with the Health Log Store (DataStore DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the transfer of personal data across a boundary, potentially violating the minimality principle if not strictly required.

title: Data in Transit
description: The health log data is transmitted between the mobile app and the health log store. Data-centric threats such as meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them may arise during this transit.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The health log store (DataStore DS1) receives and processes the health data. The destination may process or store the data in a way that causes a threat, such as retaining unnecessary personal data or making it available for further processing.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The process (P2) writes GPS location traces with timestamps to the data store (DS2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the process transfers personal data (GPS location traces) to a known third party (the data store).
assumptions: The data store is a known third party.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The data flow (DF5) transmits GPS location traces with timestamps in transit. This is a data-centric threat where the data itself (meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them) is exposed during transmission.
assumptions: The data flow transmits data-centric information.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The data store (DS2) receives the GPS location traces with timestamps. The store processes or stores this data, which may cause a threat if the data is used for purposes beyond its intended storage.
assumptions: The data store processes the received data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Log Store (DS1) shares personal health data (calorie, weight, exercise logs) with the Health Analytics Service (P3) for health-condition analysis. This constitutes a data disclosure as the data is transferred across a boundary to a third party (the analytics service) for processing.
assumptions: The data is considered personal health information.

title: Linking/Identification Threat
description: The data flow (DF6) carries meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., user IDs, session IDs, or data identifiers) that could be used to link or identify the data subjects. This is a data-centric threat arising from the transmission of identifying information.
assumptions: The data flow includes metadata that could be used for identification.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) receives the health data and processes it for health-condition analysis. This processing action may lead to the disclosure of the data to third parties or for storage purposes, constituting a data disclosure threat.
assumptions: The analytics service processes the data for health analysis, which may involve sharing or storing it.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The data store (DS2) shares location history data with the Health Analytics Service (P3). This constitutes a data disclosure as the transfer of personal data (location history) across a boundary to a third party (the analytics service) for processing. This is an explicit disclosure intended by design.
assumptions: The data store is configured to share this specific data set with the analytics service.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The data flow (DF7) carries location history data in transit from the data store to the analytics service. This data-centric threat arises from the metadata associated with the data flow, which may identify the parties involved (e.g., the data store and the analytics service) or reveal the nature of the data being transferred.
assumptions: The data flow metadata includes identifiers or descriptions that could be used to link or identify the data store and the analytics service.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The destination element (P3) receives the location history data and processes it to derive daily routine and movement patterns. This processing action may involve storing or analyzing the data in a way that causes a threat, as the analytics service is processing personal location data.
assumptions: The analytics service is processing the location history data to derive personal insights.

title: Profiling a group of individuals
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) processes health-condition risk indicators and routine summaries, which are personal data related to specific data subjects. By aggregating these indicators, the service infers insights about a larger group of individuals (e.g., a cohort of patients with similar conditions), constituting a profiling activity. This creates a risk where the identity of the data subject is linked to a broader group, potentially violating privacy principles regarding the minimization of data and the protection of individual privacy.
assumptions: The data returned by P3 is treated as personal data and is used for group-level analysis.

title: Data processing causing threat
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) receives the inferred health insights from P3. The threat arises at the destination because the app processes this data in a way that causes a privacy threat. Specifically, the app may use the aggregated group insights to identify or link individuals, or store the data in a manner that compromises the privacy of the data subjects (e.g., by making the data subject identifiable through the group profile). This destination-based threat is grounded in the data-centric nature of the threat.
assumptions: The app's processing of the health insights leads to a privacy risk.

title: Unauthorized Access to Dashboard Data
description: The process (P2) shares aggregated trend and condition indicator data (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) to the external entity (EE1). This interaction is valid (Process->ExternalEntity), but the data contains sensitive inferred health information. If the process does not implement appropriate access controls or encryption, an unauthorized party could access this data, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: The process P2 is configured to share this data with the external entity EE1.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow (DF9) transmits metadata about the parties involved (the process P2 and the external entity EE1) to the destination. This meta-data could be used to link or identify the specific individuals receiving the data, even if the data itself is encrypted. This is a data-centric threat where the act of transmitting identifies the data recipients.
assumptions: The data flow transmits metadata identifying the parties involved.

title: Unauthorized Processing of Inferred Health Data
description: The destination (EE1) receives the data and processes or stores it in a way that causes a threat. The external entity is likely to use the inferred condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) for decision-making or reporting. If the external entity does not have appropriate safeguards (e.g., data minimization, encryption, access controls), the processing of this sensitive inferred health data could lead to privacy violations.
assumptions: The external entity EE1 processes the data for its own purposes.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) shares analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset with the Cloud Hosting Provider (EE2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the data is transferred across a boundary to a third party.
assumptions: The data transfer is intended and designed as part of the service's replication and hosting capabilities.

title: Linking/Identification Threat
description: Data-centric threats arise at the data flow (fl) where meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them is transmitted. The transfer of the full health and location dataset may include metadata that allows the Cloud Hosting Provider to identify or link the data to specific individuals.
assumptions: The dataset includes metadata that could be used for identification.
uncertainty_note: Confident that metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them is transmitted during the data flow.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Cloud Hosting Provider (EE2) receives the data and processes or stores it in a way that causes the threat. As an external entity, EE2 may store or process the data in a manner that exposes it to unauthorized access or misuse, constituting a data disclosure.
assumptions: The Cloud Hosting Provider stores or processes the data in a way that causes the threat.
